title: Trace completed Core2 handoff cycles and reconcile current project state

execution.environment: macOS 26.5.1 arm64, Python 3.13.15, QEMU 9.2.2 virtual Core2

checks.name: exact_time_state_sweep
checks.detail: Three isolated virtual-time samples captured both vCPUs, handoff flags, DPORT/cache, SSI and cross-core counters.

checks.name: completed_handoff_setters
checks.detail: The first normal-WDT boot recorded about 4,376 complete/can-start handoff cycles before reset.

checks.name: cpu1_forward_progress
checks.detail: CPU1 PC and SSI/cross-core counters continued changing while CPU0 waited.

checks.name: permanent_handoff_deadlock
checks.detail: Repeated completed setter cycles and controller activity do not support a single permanently stuck handoff.

checks.name: uart_storm
checks.detail: The prior UART/VM mapping remains rejected by BIN/ELF byte audit and is not reintroduced.

checks.name: stage0_timeout_recovery
checks.detail: The first stage-0 timeout at 5.913935 seconds is not followed by restored WDT feed/service progress.

checks.name: legacy_application
checks.detail: No REPL or non-empty application frame; the first WDT reset occurs at 15.914787 seconds.

notes: The full UIFlow2 matrix was not rerun after 0039/0040.
No matching ELF/MAP was available for the public legacy BIN.
The retained dirty QEMU worktree must not be reset or cleaned.
All functional results are virtual-device validation.
